albums.blurb: Tyler is a Nashville guitarist who came up as a sideman in Lambchop and Silver Jews before establishing himself as one of the leading voices in the John Fahey lineage of solo steel-string composition. Modern Country, his fourth album and first for Merge, was also his first recorded outside Nashville: he cut it at April Base Studios in Wisconsin with a full band including multi-instrumentalist Phil Cook, bassist Darin Gray, and Wilco percussionist Glenn Kotche, expanding his fingerpicked pieces into pastoral, slowly building ensemble arrangements. The record is entirely instrumental, conceived as a meditation on the vanishing American landscape of back highways and dying small towns.
albums.reception: The album landed on several year-end lists in 2016, including the number 4 spot on Magnet's top albums of the year and Rolling Stone Country's best country albums of 2016.

albums.blurb: Apricot Princess is the second album by Alex O'Connor, the English songwriter behind Rex Orange County, self-released in April 2017 when he was 18. Written and largely performed by O'Connor himself, it sets diaristic love songs to jazz chords, strings, and soul grooves, moving between piano balladry and brighter full-band pop across ten tracks. It arrived just months before his guest turns on Tyler, the Creator's Flower Boy introduced him to a much wider audience, and it remains the clearest statement of his early jazz-school-dropout style.
albums.reception: The self-released album reached number 2 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart and number 8 on the US Independent Albums chart, and O'Connor was voted runner-up in the BBC Sound of 2018 poll on the strength of it.

albums.blurb: Mayfield spent the 1960s leading The Impressions, writing civil-rights-era standards like "People Get Ready," before launching a solo career with this September 1970 debut on his own Curtom label. Curtis stretches his falsetto soul into longer, heavier forms — orchestral arrangements, Latin and psychedelic percussion, and pointed social commentary on "(Don't Worry) If There's a Hell Below, We're All Going to Go" and the horn-driven "Move On Up." Its blend of socially conscious lyrics with expansive soul-funk arrangements preceded and helped clear the path for Marvin Gaye's What's Going On and Stevie Wonder's Innervisions.
albums.reception: The album was certified gold, peaked at number 19 on the Billboard pop albums chart while topping the R&B albums chart, and was ranked number 275 on Rolling Stone's 2020 edition of the 500 Greatest Albums of All Time.
